# @zakkster/lite-overlap

> Zero-GC persistent overlap events over a dynamic BVH (2D). Turns "who overlaps
> now" into a per-frame *delta* -- who just started overlapping (enter), who is
> still touching (stay), who just stopped (exit) -- and finds every pair once in a
> single tree self-traversal. Layer filtering cuts cost without changing results,
> and swept detection catches a projectile that tunnels through a thin trigger in
> one frame. **No allocations after construction, on any frame path.** Companion
> to `@zakkster/lite-bvh` and `@zakkster/lite-aabb` (same `FORMAT_VERSION` buffer
> contract; no runtime dependency, format agreement only).

Version `1.3.0`. Named exports: `createOverlap`, `VERSION`, `FORMAT_VERSION`.

`FORMAT_VERSION` (integer, currently `1`) is the shared buffer-contract version.
`@zakkster/lite-aabb` and `@zakkster/lite-bvh` export the identical constant; a
conformance test asserts all three equal. It is on a separate axis from the semver
`VERSION` and is copied inline (no runtime dependency on the peers).

It is **not a solver.** No contact normals, no minimum translation vector, no
impulses. It owns the layer between a spatial index and game logic: pair
lifecycle, all-pairs detection in one descent, layer filtering that cuts cost
without changing results, and (this release) swept detection so a fast projectile
cannot pass through a trigger unseen.

## Model

A frame is `begin()` -> zero or more pair reports -> `end()`. A pair is reported
either by traversing a BVH (`collectPairs(tree)`) or by hand (`add(a, b)`), or
both into the same frame. After `end()`, read the delta with
`drainEnter` / `drainExit`. Ids are non-negative int32 `userData` values (the
`@zakkster/lite-bvh` contract); `-1` is the empty-slot sentinel and must never be
passed to `add`.

## API

```ts
// ALLOCATES -- call at setup. maxPairs is a positive integer; every buffer is
// sized from it. A new distinct pair past the cap throws atomically (table
// unchanged, still usable); read stats().highWaterMark to size it. maxEntityId
// (optional) caps the userData-keyed filter arrays: given => fixed + fail-closed
// above it; omitted => those arrays grow lazily-once on the cold setLayer/
// setEnabled path (never on a frame), so a caller who never filters pays nothing.
function createOverlap(options: { maxPairs: number, maxEntityId?: number }): Overlap;

interface Overlap {
    // Open a frame: flip the internal tag so every slot's stamp is now stale,
    // bump the telemetry epoch, clear the enter/exit staging. O(1).
    begin(): void;

    // Report a candidate overlapping pair. HOT: one hash, one probe, one tag
    // write -- no string/object/closure. Order-invariant ((a,b)==(b,a)) and
    // idempotent within a frame. a===b is rejected. THROWS atomically if a new
    // distinct pair would exceed maxPairs (reserve-before-mutate).
    add(a: number, b: number): void;

    // All-pairs self-traversal over a BVH's readonly SoA, feeding add() directly
    // -- find every overlapping pair ONCE, no query-box rebuilds. Reports the
    // tree's FAT-bound pairs: conservative (a reported pair's tight boxes may not
    // overlap; a real overlap is never missed). Recheck with narrow() and YOUR
    // tight boxes before acting on geometry. Zero allocation on the traversal
    // path (fixed node-pair stack sized from tree.maxNodes; fail-closed throw on
    // an impossible overflow, never grows). Call between begin() and end().
    collectPairs(tree: BvhTreeView): void;

    // SWEPT self-traversal (this release): the tunneling fix. Tests the swept
    // volume union(prev, curr) instead of the instantaneous box, so a projectile
    // faster than its own width no longer crosses a thin trigger unseen. Feeds
    // add() and the ordinary lifecycle -- a pass-through fires ENTER this frame,
    // EXIT the next; no new drain to wire. PRECONDITION: tree leaf boxes must
    // BOUND the swept motion -- build them as fatten(union(prev, curr)) (else the
    // descent prunes the tunneling pair before the refinement can see it). Each
    // leaf pair is refined with the tight union from prevPacked/currPacked (packed
    // 4*count, userData-indexed); a leaf userData >= count is fail-closed. Superset
    // of collectPairs, and byte-identical to it when prevPacked === currPacked
    // (zero motion). The layer filter applies identically. Zero allocation.
    collectSweptPairs(tree: BvhTreeView, prevPacked: Float32Array,
                      currPacked: Float32Array, count: number): void;

    // The manual swept pair door -- the swept analog of add(a, b): records the pair
    // iff the two entities' swept volumes overlap. The differential oracle for
    // collectSweptPairs. UNFILTERED, like add. Boxes are Float32Array(4).
    addSwept(a: number, prevBoxA: Float32Array, currBoxA: Float32Array,
             b: number, prevBoxB: Float32Array, currBoxB: Float32Array): void;

    // Close the frame: one linear table scan emits an exit for every pair present
    // last frame but not touched this frame, and removes it. O(capacity).
    end(): void;

    // LAYERS / FILTERS (this release). All cold-config; filtering is applied
    // inside collectPairs, before add, and changes COST not results (a filtered
    // pair simply is not re-stamped and exits via end()). State is sampled at
    // collect -- set it BEFORE the frame's collectPairs. With none of these ever
    // called, collectPairs runs the exact unfiltered path (identity).

    // Assign an entity to a layer [0,31] (default 0). Keyed by userData, so it
    // survives BVH rotations (a refit relinks node ids, never userData).
    setLayer(userData: number, layerIndex: number): void;

    // Set whether two layers interact. Sets BOTH (a,b) and (b,a) -- the 32x32
    // matrix is symmetric by construction. Default: all pairs enabled (identity).
    setInteract(layerA: number, layerB: number, enabled: boolean): void;

    // Enable/disable an entity. A disabled entity generates no pairs; its live
    // pairs all fire exit at the next end(), exactly once, via the mark-sweep.
    setEnabled(userData: number, enabled: boolean): void;

    // Copy this frame's enter / exit ids into caller buffers (bvh query(out)
    // convention; canonically ordered outA[k] < outB[k]). Non-destructive until
    // the next begin(). Returns the count, capped at the shorter buffer.
    drainEnter(outA: Int32Array, outB: Int32Array): number;
    drainExit(outA: Int32Array, outB: Int32Array): number;

    pairCount(): number;    // live pairs in the table
    stayCount(): number;    // live pairs that did not enter this frame

    // Diagnostic snapshot (cold path; allocates one plain object by design).
    // highWaterMark -> size maxPairs from it; stackHighWater -> the traversal
    // frontier high-water; epoch -> plain-number frame counter (telemetry only).
    stats(): {
        pairCount: number; stayCount: number; capacity: number;
        loadFactor: number; probeHighWater: number; highWaterMark: number;
        stackHighWater: number; epoch: number;
    };

    // Silently empty the table without reallocating and WITHOUT emitting exits.
    // To flush exits on teardown, run one empty begin(); end(); then clear().
    clear(): void;
}

// The tight recheck. A BVH stores only FATTENED boxes, so only YOU hold the tight
// geometry -- narrow takes your two tight boxes, not the tree. Pure boolean AABB
// overlap; zero allocation, zero dependency. Run it on a pair collectPairs
// reported, before you act.
function narrow(boxA: Float32Array, boxB: Float32Array): boolean;   // [minX,minY,maxX,maxY]

// The pure swept predicate -- the swept analog of narrow. Whether the swept volume
// of A (union of its prev and curr tight boxes) overlaps the swept volume of B.
// Conservative (over-reports on diagonal motion, never misses); zero allocation.
function sweptOverlap(prevA: Float32Array, currA: Float32Array,
                     prevB: Float32Array, currB: Float32Array): boolean;

// The readonly BVH view collectPairs reads (a @zakkster/lite-bvh instance
// satisfies it as-is): bboxes (4*maxNodes), children (2*maxNodes, -1/-1 at a
// leaf), heights (0 at a leaf), userData (leaf id, -1 internal), root, maxNodes.
interface BvhTreeView { /* see Overlap.d.ts */ }
```

## Layers / filters -- cost down, results unchanged

Give entities a layer with `setLayer(id, layer)` and turn layer pairs on/off with
`setInteract(a, b, on)` (a symmetric 32x32 matrix, all-on by default). At each
leaf-leaf candidate `collectPairs` mask-tests the two endpoints before `add`, so
filtered pairs are never recorded -- strictly cheaper than filtering the emitted
set after. Filtering is **results-preserving**: the filtered set equals the
unfiltered set post-filtered in JS, always. Because state is keyed by `userData`
(never a node id), it stays correct across BVH rotations -- a per-node cached mask
would silently go stale on the next refit, so this package does not keep one.
`setEnabled(id, false)` is the special case that removes all of an entity's pairs;
each fires exit exactly once, on the frame it is disabled, through the ordinary
mark-sweep. Set any filter BEFORE the frame's `collectPairs`; it is sampled there.

## Swept detection -- a trigger you can shoot through is a bug

A projectile moving faster than its own width is in front of a thin trigger at
frame N and behind it at frame N+1: the overlap existed at no sampled instant, and
discrete detection misses it. `addSwept` (manual) and `collectSweptPairs` (bulk)
test the swept volume -- the AABB `union(prev, curr)` -- instead of the
instantaneous box, so the crossing is caught. Both feed the same `add` door and
lifecycle, so a pass-through fires **enter** on the crossing frame through the
ordinary `drainEnter` channel and **exit** the next; there is no separate event to
wire up and no pair is silently missed. The swept set is always a **superset** of
the discrete set (the union contains `curr`), and with zero motion
(`prevPacked === currPacked`) it is byte-identical to `collectPairs`.

`collectSweptPairs` has one caller contract: the tree's leaf boxes must **bound
the swept motion** -- build them as `fatten(union(prev, curr))` (use
`aabb2.merge` / `mergeAll`; that batch op is the caller's tree-build, not a
runtime dependency of this package). Otherwise the descent prunes the tunneling
pair before the refinement runs. The refinement recomputes the tight
`union(prev, curr)` from the packed motion arrays, indexed by `userData`, and
drops the fattening's over-reports -- exactly as `narrow` refines the discrete
path. The union is conservative on diagonal motion (it is the bounding rectangle
of the thin diagonal sweep ribbon): never a missed pair, but recheck geometry with
your own tight boxes before acting. At world-scale coordinates a motion delta
below the local float32 ULP is swallowed (finding A-01); keep the delta -- or a
`fatten` margin -- above `aabb2.marginFloor(box)` so the swept volume stays
strictly larger than its endpoints.

## Fat vs tight -- the one thing to get right

`collectPairs` reports the boxes the tree holds, which a BVH keeps *fattened* for
cheap refit. So it is a broadphase: it never misses a real overlap, but it can
report a near-miss. If you fire damage, a pickup, or a sound on `onEnter` from the
raw pair, add a `narrow(yourTightA, yourTightB)` gate first. The tree cannot give
you the tight answer -- it does not store tight boxes -- so you pass your own.

## Guarantees

- Zero runtime dependencies. Single ESM file. `sideEffects: false`.
- Zero allocation on every frame path: `add`, `collectPairs`, `end`, the drains,
  and `narrow`. Proven by a `node --expose-gc` torture gate at
  `maxMajor: 0`, `maxArrayBuffersGrowth: 0`, with a `Set<string>` control that
  must fail the gate (so the gate is falsifiable).
- Fail closed on every unverified state: capacity exhaustion, stack overflow, and
  a corrupt tree (leaf signals that disagree) all throw with a remedy, never
  silently mis-report.
